source.title: The Multiscale Structure of Neural Network Loss Functions: The Effect on Optimization and Origin
source.authors: Chao Ma; D. Kunin; Lei Wu; Le-Xing Ying

record.file_problem: The supplied text is the full paper. The title in the text differs slightly from the catalog title; no other document problem noted.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports a neural-network training experiment measuring sharpness and training loss around the edge of stability, relevant to V5. It does not test the specific above-initial-linearized-stability learning-rate recipe in V5.
record.gate_note: The paper also reports learning-rate-decay experiments and loss-landscape visualizations, but those do not test the listed claim versions. Its theoretical analyses use simplified objective functions, not neural-network training results.
record.test_reason: Figure 1 reports the study's own GD experiment measuring Hessian sharpness and training loss, directly testing V5's edge-of-stability component with the same method and measures as Cohen et al.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately captures the edge-of-stability conclusion but incompletely summarizes the paper. The authors argue that observed subquadratic loss growth can explain edge-of-stability dynamics, separate scales can explain learning-rate-decay behavior, and constructive examples show how nonconvex models and nonuniform training data can generate multiscale losses.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies loss landscapes and edge-of-stability behavior; it does not use the learning-rate recipes specified in V5.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper shows different training-loss and test-accuracy curves when learning-rate decay occurs at epoch 250 versus epoch 500.

fits_no_version.finding: Learning-rate decay timing changes training trajectories and generalization; gradient-direction landscape slices show subquadratic growth in VGG11, ResNet18 and DenseNet121.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Multiscale loss landscapes help explain learning-rate decay and bounded oscillatory GD dynamics.

record.peer_reviewed: Journal of Machine Learning (as stated in the catalog; the supplied text identifies itself as an arXiv preprint)
record.problems: The relevant neural-network edge-of-stability result is a single example shown in Figure 1, without numerical values or uncertainty estimates. The paper does not report the squared-loss wide-network recipe specified by V5.
record.rows_left_out: No rows were retained: the paper's relevant edge-of-stability measurements are displayed only as curves in Figure 1, and the text provides no numerical values to record. The remaining results do not measure a listed version.

untested.parts: Near-zero training classification error, random or corrupted labels, and model-size or training-recipe comparisons.
Teacher-student spurious-minimum frequencies and the effect of extra student neurons.
Depth-related training degradation and comparisons involving identity shortcuts or normalization.
Initialization-dependent training speed and trainable depth.
The wide-network squared-loss catapult regime, initial loss rise and curvature drop, divergence at larger rates, and divergence despite starting below the stability threshold.
Batch-normalization effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, including Fixup comparisons.

missing.what: Qualitative observed rows for sharpness increasing and stabilizing near 2/η, and training loss continuing to decrease afterward, in the three-layer fully connected CIFAR-10 experiment. The declared omission for lack of precise numerical values should be corrected: the caption and text explicitly establish these outcomes.

record.verdict_notes: This study is not an original source listed for V5. Its simplified-objective theorems explain a possible mechanism; they do not independently establish the untested neural-network regimes in V5. The empirical support is one example without reported uncertainty or precise curve values.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error, CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 error, random or corrupted labels, model size, and training duration.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems, spurious minima frequency, and width differences.
Depth comparisons, identity shortcuts, and training error with or without normalization.

The paper does not test the squared-loss wide-network recipe above the initial linearized stability limit, rate-dependent divergence, or runs starting below the stability threshold. It reports one edge-of-stability experiment but the relevant values are shown in a figure without numerical values.
Batch-normalization comparisons of training speed or learning-rate tolerance.

relationships.condition: GD training of a three-layer fully connected network on a CIFAR-10 subset.
relationships.reason: Figure 1 left and Section 2.1 explicitly report sharpness rising to approximately 2/η and remaining there while training loss continues falling; verdict rests on the text because no rows were extracted.
relationships.display_finding: Sharpness rose to approximately 2/η and remained there while training loss continued falling.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
